kitDescription: Sakura Suzuhara is a Water SMG Supporter whose entire offensive contribution is a recurring boss debuff: after landing 120 normal attacks (exactly one of her 120-round magazines), the boss takes 17.18% increased damage for 5 seconds, refreshing once per magazine cycle at roughly 75-80% uptime. Her Skill 2 is pure sustain — every 60 hits she boosts incoming healing on the 2 lowest-HP allies, and every 120 hits she cuts the damage those 2 allies take by about 15%. Her Burst I is a heal-over-time that restores 10.03% of her own max HP to the 2 lowest-HP allies every second for 10 seconds. She has no damage lines of her own; in a damage sim her value is the team-wide damage-taken debuff's uptime plus the recovery-event stream that feeds teammates' on-heal triggers.

skill1.driverSaid: hitCount:120 → target enemy → buff damageTakenPct 17.18 / durationSec 5; boss-held (targetIdx null), refreshes per KR overwrite rule, ~79% uptime at one proc per magazine
skill1.blindSaid: S2b FAITHFUL (load-bearing); S6 blind override reproduces the block line-for-line (hitCount 120 / enemy / 17.18 / 5s)
skill1.formulaCheck: damageTakenPct routes to the Taken bucket (SSOT §1g '1 + Σ Damage Taken ▲ on the boss') — correct bucket, correct boss scope, correct 5s wall-clock semantics; hitCount is the prose-stated primitive, NOT lastBullet (coincides at ammo 120 but diverges under ammo modifiers — correctly avoided)
skill1.explanation: Driver test pins count === floor(shots/120), first apply > t=0, exact 5*60 frame expiry, team damage drop on removal, and discriminates vs a passive always-on counterfactual. The fired-vs-landed hitCount semantics gap is a documented ⚑ (caveat with estimate + recipe), matching the repo convention for 'after landing N normal attacks'.

skill2.driverSaid: UNMODELED verbatim in unmodeled.skill2; caveat: no healing-received StatKey exists and heal effects carry no HP amount, so the amplifier multiplies nothing; nearest-wrong (encoding as a heal effect every 60 hits → spurious recovery events feeding crown-class consumers) explicitly rejected
skill2.blindSaid: S2b UNMODELED; S5 it.skip with the same GAP reasoning; S6 unmodeled verbatim
skill2.formulaCheck: No schema channel for received-healing scaling; inert at scope lock; the rejected nearest-wrong would over-credit recovery consumers at SMG cadence — correctly not encoded
skill2.explanation: Deliberate, documented, and pinned by negative assertions (nothing may come out of the skill2 slot; byte-identical totals under strip).

skill2.driverSaid: UNMODELED verbatim; ⚑ caveat: ally received-damage mitigation with no ally HP pool / no incoming boss damage in v1; estimate + recipe + tier (engine-core, out-of-domain) supplied; explicitly refuses to misuse the boss-facing damageTakenPct channel (wrong direction/target — would manufacture a phantom ~15% team damage change on the same 120-hit frame as S1)
skill2.blindSaid: S2b UNMODELED — flagged as THE kit trap (twin 'Damage Taken' lines firing on the same frame); S5 requires exactly one boss-held apply of exactly 17.18 per proc, never ±14.97 or a stacked 32.15; S6 unmodeled verbatim
skill2.formulaCheck: Taken bucket is boss-side only (SSOT §1g); an ally-side ▼ has no engine primitive and the boss deals no damage in v1 — unmodelable by construction; the conflation trap is neutralized by value+count pins
skill2.explanation: The highest-risk line in the kit is handled exactly right: documented, flagged with a recipe, and pinned so neither a +14.97 nor −14.97 boss encoding can pass.

burst.driverSaid: burstCast → alliesLowestHp count:2 → heal ticks:10 intervalSec:1; recovery-EVENT cadence is the modeled substance (helm H2 precedent), the 10.03%-of-final-Max-HP magnitude inherently unmodeled (no HP pool) and documented
burst.blindSaid: S2b FAITHFUL (load-bearing: the recovery events, not the HP number); S6 blind override reproduces the block line-for-line
burst.formulaCheck: 'every 1 sec for 10 sec' → ticks:10 intervalSec:1 matches the documented HoT encoding; trigger correctly burstCast (her own cast) not fullBurstEnter — the contention arm with liter proves liter-opened FBs emit zero recovery stream; heal feeds recovery triggers per the taxonomy-#4 rule
burst.explanation: Driver pins ≥3 casts/180s, exactly 10 ticks × N allies per cast, 1s spacing across the 9*60-frame window, and discriminates vs ticks:1 (exactly 1/10 the events) and vs fullBurstEnter (heals appear on liter-opened rotations). The alliesLowestHp → leftmost-2 stand-in is a documented engine convention, not a kit misread.

verdictRationale: No real gotchas: both blind re-derivations converged mechanically — the S6 blind override reproduces the driver's shipped override line-for-line (same skill1 block, same burst block, same two verbatim unmodeled skill2 lines), and the adapted S5 blind suite is fully GREEN against the shipped override; the only S5 as-authored failures were fixture masking on the blind side (helm's saturating heals hiding the crown consumer in BOTH arms — the known helm H8 isolation problem), classified as a blind-fixture recon artifact, not a driver divergence. All four kit lines are FAITHFUL (S1 boss debuff — right Taken bucket, right hitCount primitive, cadence-pinned and counterfactual-discriminated; burst HoT — right burstCast identity proven under B1 contention with liter) or DOCUMENTED_GAP (both skill2 lines, verbatim in unmodeled with the twin-'Damage Taken' conflation trap explicitly rejected and negative-pinned, plus an estimate/recipe/tier ⚑ on the ally mitigation line). Every load-bearing test discriminates against its named nearest-wrong model (passive-S1, ticks:1, fullBurstEnter, stripped slots), and each FAITHFUL block demonstrably fires at the prose-implied cadence (floor(shots/120) debuff applies; 10 recovery ticks per cast). What must change for GO: nothing. Same-model residual for the owner to spot-check: the hitCount fired-vs-landed semantics (engine counts fired rounds; prose says landed — both blind agents and the driver adopted the repo convention and flagged it, so a real over-credit of the debuff duty cycle could hide in plain sight) and the always-⚑ SMG cadence tuple, which scales her entire contribution 1:1.
